title: Cyrus's Decree and the Return
summary: In Cyrus's first year the LORD moves the king of Persia to proclaim that he has been charged to build him a house in Jerusalem and that any of God's people may go up, while neighbors help with silver, gold and goods. Cyrus returns the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar took, counted out to Sheshbazzar. Chapter 2 lists those who go up under Zerubbabel and Jeshua, about 42,360 plus servants, and records the gifts made toward the house.

title: Rebuilding the Altar and Foundation
summary: In the seventh month the returnees gather at Jerusalem, and Jeshua and Zerubbabel rebuild the altar on its base and offer burnt offerings despite fear of the peoples around them, and they keep the Feast of Tabernacles. In the second year Levites are appointed to oversee the work, and when the foundation is laid, priests and Levites praise the LORD with trumpets and cymbals. Older people who had seen the first house weep aloud while others shout for joy, and the noise carries far.

title: Opposition and Delay
summary: Adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ask to join the building, claiming to worship the same God, but Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse. The people of the land then discourage the Jews and hire counselors to frustrate them through the reigns of Cyrus and Darius. Under Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes they send letters accusing the Jews of rebuilding a rebellious city, and Artaxerxes orders the work stopped, which Rehum and Shimshai enforce by force. Work on the temple ceases until Darius's second year.

title: The Temple Completed
summary: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah urge the Jews to resume building, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua do so. Tatnai, governor beyond the river, writes to Darius, who has the archives searched, finds Cyrus's decree, and orders that the work proceed at the royal expense and that opponents be punished. The temple is finished in Darius's sixth year, dedicated with joy and a hundred bulls, and the priests and Levites are set in their courses. The people keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread.

title: Ezra Comes to Jerusalem
summary: Ezra, a priest and skilled scribe descended from Aaron, goes up from Babylon in Artaxerxes's seventh year with a royal letter granting silver, gold and supplies, and authority to appoint judges and teach the law. At the river Ahava he gathers about 1,500 men and finds no Levites, so he sends for Levites. Ashamed to ask the king for soldiers, he proclaims a fast to seek a safe journey, and the company reaches Jerusalem after four months and delivers the treasure.

title: Ezra and Mixed Marriages
summary: Leaders tell Ezra that many of the people, priests and Levites have married women of the surrounding peoples. Ezra tears his clothes, pulls hair from his head, and sits appalled until the evening sacrifice, then prays and confesses Israel's guilt. As he weeps, a large crowd gathers; Shechaniah proposes a covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children. The people assemble in the rain and agree, and officials examine each case over three months. A list names those involved.
